sentences.text: Appearance:

Shri Himanshu Paliwal, learned counsel for the appellan
 Shri Anil Kumar Goyal, learned counsel for respondent N
 Company.
 Order

The appellants have filed this Misc. Appeal under Section 173(1) of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 being aggrieved by the award dated 13.07.2023 passed by the XI Member, Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Indore (M.P.) in Claim Case No.257/2021.
2.
The issue regarding the accident and the liability of the Insurance Company is not in dispute.
3. The brief facts of the case are that on 14.07.2020, the deceased Mukesh along with his friends was going on motorcycle from his home to Devsiraliya.

When they reached the area near Krishna Gaushala, a vehicle bearing registration number MP-41-MH-7383, which was being driven rashly and negligently, dashed into the motorcycle of the deceased Mukesh.
As a result, he sustained grievous injuries to his head and other parts of his body.
He was rushed to the Government Hospital in Kannod in 108 Ambulence, from where he was referred to Dewas.

Due to the severity of his injuries, he was further referred to M.Y. Hospital in NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2025:MPHC-IND:20975 2 MA-7167-2023 Indore and later again to Synergy Hospital.
However, he succumbed to his injuries during the treatment.

3.1. The appellants / claimants filed their claim petition under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act,
1988 before the Claims Tribunal for the death of the deceased Mukesh in the aforesaid accident.

The Claims Tribunal, after assessing the evidence on record, concluded that the just and proper amount of compensation for loss of dependency would be Rs.15,75,560/- and after awarding compensation under other heads, a total compensation of Rs.17,40,560/- was awarded to the appellants.

4. Learned counsel for Insurance Company supports the findings of the Claims Tribunal and Reenabai vs The New India Insurance Co. Ltd. on 6 August, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/62457444/
1 submits that no inference is warranted with the award passed by the Claims Tribunal.
5. Heard learned counsel for the respective parties and perused the record.

entities.text: Reenabai vs The New India Insurance Co. Ltd.
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 6. Counsel for the appellants submits that there are five claimants: the wife, son, daughter, mother and father of the deceased.

The Claims Tribunal has not accounted for the mother and father in assessing the amount of compensation, based on the admission by Reenabai (AW-1) in her cross-examination that the mother and father of the deceased were living separately and bearing their own expenses.
In any case, it has not been established that the mother and father of the deceased were earning members.
Even if it is accepted, based on the testimony of AW-1, that the father was not dependent on the income of the son, the son must have been contributing to the well-being of his mother.
Thus, it cannot be said that the mother was not dependent on the income of the deceased Mukesh.
Therefore, the mother of the deceased should be considered as one of the dependents.

As a result, the number of dependents is four and in accordance with the law laid down NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-IND:20975 3 MA-7167-2023 in the case of National Insurance Company Ltd. vs. Pranay Sethi reported in 2017 ACJ 2700, in the case of four dependents, the deduction for personal expenses should be made at 1/4 of the income of the deceased.

entities.text: National Insurance Company Ltd. vs. Pranay Sethi reported in 2017 ACJ 2700
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Consequently, the compensation for loss of dependency would be Rs.17,72,505/-.
7.

Furthermore, it is observed that the Claims Tribunal has not awarded compensation for loss of consortium to the mother and father, whereas, in view of the law laid down in the case of Magma General Insurance Co. Ltd. Vs. Nanu Ram, 2019 ACJ SC 2782 , both of them are entitled to compensation for filial consortium, which amounts to Rs.88,000/-,

entities.text: Magma General Insurance Co. Ltd. Vs. Nanu Ram, 2019 ACJ SC 2782
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Thus, the total the compensation would come to Rs.20,25,505/-.
8.
The Claims Tribunal has already awarded Rs.17,40,560/-.
Therefore, the appellants are now entitled to additional compensation of Rs.2,84,945/- over and above the amount already awarded by the Claims Tribunal.
9. The enhanced amount shall carry interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of filing of the application before the Claims Tribunal.
10. In view of the above, the present appeal is allowed.
